title: Flowable's engine issues UPDATE against its own history table
content:
`HistoricProcessInstance.xml` defines `updateHistoricProcessInstance`, issuing `update ${prefix}ACT_HI_PROCINST` with `REV_`, `PROC_DEF_ID_`, `BUSINESS_KEY_` and `START_TIME_` among the assignable columns. Equivalent update mappers exist for historic task and activity instances.

The presence of a `REV_` optimistic-locking column is the strongest signal: rows carrying a revision counter are rows expected to change. This is mutability established from the engine's own source rather than inferred from the absence of a guarantee.

It also makes the sharpest possible demonstration. A hand-written `UPDATE` against that table is indistinguishable from the engine's own behaviour — same statement shape, same revision increment, no gap and no tamper indicator — because legitimate rewrites are how the component works.
description: The MyBatis mapper for HistoricProcessInstance rewrites START_TIME_ and BUSINESS_KEY_ in place, with a REV_ optimistic-locking column indicating the row is designed for mutation.
